records.real_world_identity_notes: BMW 2002 turbo of 1973 to 1975, the 170 PS turbocharged 02, offered with a strengthened Getrag 232 four-speed unique to the turbo or the optional Getrag 235/5 close-ratio five-speed.
records.confidence_basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by a registered source.
records.identity_basis: A registered source establishes the 2002 turbo and its gearbox options, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
records.specification_basis: The source gives a four-speed or an optional Getrag 235/5 five-speed, and the live drive selected five H-pattern gears, which is the five-speed of that pair.
records.confidence_notes: Guided testing directly established the gear count, the standing-start clutch, the clutchless running shifts, and the automatic cut and blip state.
control_notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift and blips to downshift.
The drive found five gears, so AMS2 models the optional Getrag 235/5 close-ratio five-speed rather than the four-speed that was standard on this car.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional rather than required, which is reserved for gearboxes that cannot engage without it.
This class reports a single configuration; the selection screen offers no aero package and only the plain identity has been observed.
